newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GOVMT BODY POSTPONES FUEL QUOTA DISCUSSION.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GOVMT BODY POSTPONES FUEL QUOTA DISCUSSION.

text.p: The Polish government's economic committee (KERM) postponed on Monday a planned discussion of a duty-free fuel imports quota, a government press office spokesman said.

Jerzy Izdebski told a news conference the KERM would return to the issue of the quota together with a discussion on freeing fuel prices, now controlled by the finance ministry. He did not say when the KERM would discuss freeign fuel prices.
"KERM will return to the issue of the duty-free quota when discussing the freeing of fuel prices," Izdebski said.

Earlier this year government officials said the freeing of fuel prices could take place at the end of this year or early in 1997, but some analysts said high world oil prices could jeopardise the implementation of the scheme at that date.

Last week Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said the quota, estimated by the market at between 300,000 and 600,000 tonnes of petrol and diesel fuel would be used to cushion the expected price jump when prices are freed.

Refineries and petrol distributors have been calling for the duty-free imports because high oil prices on world markets combined with government caps on fuel prices made domestic production unprofitable, causing shortages in some regions.

The government does not want to allow higher fuel prices because it wants to avoid the inflationary impluse it would create, possibly threatening the 17 percent year-on-year target for December 1996 against 21.6 percent in December 1995.
